posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **patrickb:** "difficult preparation." hummm wonder what this means???

Rallison doesn't talk about it, as far as I'm aware. The quote merely goes as follows: "....Pyridine dichromate. We don't use it because of its shorter shelf life and difficult preparation." If he says it's difficult, then it doesn't bode well. 

Also check Shankoff, 1968: "The source of Cr2O7 was either (NH4)2Cr2O7 or the pyridine-dichromate complex (PDC), which crystallizes when a saturated aqueous solution of 5ml of pyridine and 7g of CrO3 is added to excess acetone maintained at -10C."

Doesn't sound good, does it?

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **patrickb:** i got it on ebay 100g for 35$http://cgi.ebay.com/Pyridinium-dichroma ... dZViewItemhummm, so i wonder with your info you have to mix it at lower temps and and lower amounts

Nice job in getting the PDC off eBay. Is the "info" you mention above the paper by Shankoff? The way I take it, that -10C figure is only given in relation to synthesizing the PDC itself, so I don't think it's relevant if you already have the PDC. I would just mix it like regular dichromate (I guess), and expose to 532nm or shorter. But note the following comments in the 1968 Applied Optics paper by Shankoff (you don't have it??):

"....Unhardened gelatin films were made from aqueous solutions of gelatin and 38 wt % PDC using a Fisher dipcoating apparatus."

Please don't ask what he means exactly by 38 wt % because I don't know!!

Also, more importantly, "....significant dark reaction occurs in PDC sensitized films in several hours."

Other than that, good luck!
